result.process_description:
Title: New Application for Registering for an USI course

If you want to register for a course at the sports institute, you need to select a course.
If slots are free, the system tells you the courses, and dates.
Select one.
Next, you need to check if you already have an account at the sports institute.
If not, you need to check whether you are registered at an eligible university.
If you are, register your account.
If you are not, request an activation and wait for a response.
As soon as you have an account, log into it.
The application is also connected to your twitter account, and lets you tweet to friends who might want to join you, you can complete the registration for the course and provide the payment information.
In the end, you will receive a course ticket.

result.rule: When the description states that a later activity is performed only if a readiness state holds, where that readiness is checked after one or more preparatory activities that run without any condition, and the description does not require those preparatory activities to be joined before the check: Model an exclusive gateway at the point where the readiness check occurs: after the preparatory activities and before the conditional activity. Give the outgoing flow to the conditional activity a condition that states the readiness requirement. Do not use a parallel gateway at this point, because it forces its branches to run and cannot express a condition. Place the gateway in the lane of the participant who checks readiness, or in the lane of the participant who performs the conditional activity if the description names no checker.

When the description states that the actor must check or verify a condition (for example whether they already hold an account, or whether they meet an eligibility criterion) and then gives alternative outcomes in an if/if-not clause: Model the check as its own task, labelled with a verb-object phrase that names the check, placed before the exclusive gateway that splits the outcomes. Use a service task if the description says the system performs the check, and a user task if the person performs it. Do not replace the check with a gateway alone.

When the description states a check of whether a person or case meets a criterion (for example 'check whether you are registered at ...'), followed by distinct outcomes introduced with 'if you are' and 'if you are not' that lead to different next steps: Model the check itself as an activity that precedes the decision, rather than omitting it. Follow that activity with an exclusive gateway that has one outgoing flow per stated outcome, and guard each flow with the condition named in the description. Keep the two outcome branches separate and give each its own following steps, and do not merge them back before their stated next steps.

When the description states that one activity is always performed, while another activity is performed only under a stated condition, and both are followed by a shared later step (the activities may run together or separately depending on the condition): Model the unconditional activity and the conditional activity as outgoing branches of one inclusive split gateway placed where the description introduces them. Guard only the conditional branch with its condition, and leave the unconditional branch without a condition. Do not place a separate exclusive decision gateway in front of the conditional activity, and do not start the unconditional activity from a parallel split that also feeds the conditional branch. Rejoin the branches with one inclusive join gateway before the shared later step, so the flow continues when either the condition holds or fails. Do not use an exclusive gateway, which allows only one branch, or a parallel gateway, which forces the conditional branch to run.
